styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small grey-blue lead weight with a ring handle. Its 15 distinct colours per full tile beat prop-hedge (10) and sit close to prop-stall-cheese (17) and prop-well-roofed (20). Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so no 5x5 block is a single colour. None of its dark edge pixels are neutral (0%), so the outline leans dark blue-grey, the tone of the neighbouring metal, rather than a uniform black sticker line. I count about 5 lightness steps on the metal, from a top highlight through the mid tones to a dark base, plus a few marks on the face. That is slightly shallower than the 6 or so on the richer references. It has only 18 colours in total, against 38-40 for the larger stall and well, but it is a much smaller single-material object, so that is expected. At this scale it would sit next to the references without looking flatter or thinner, so I pass it. The small size limits how much I can verify by eye, but the measured facts support the pass.
